title: Python Inheritance and Method Overriding
learningObjectives: Explain the core concepts of Python Inheritance and Method Overriding.
Choose an appropriate object-oriented design for a small Python problem.
Trace object state and method calls accurately.
Apply Python class features with correct method and attribute behavior.
Recognize design trade-offs, edge cases and maintainability concerns.

understand.concept: Inheritance creates a subclass from a base class, allowing it to reuse and specialize behavior. A subclass can override methods and use super() to cooperate with the next implementation in the method resolution order. Prefer composition when a type is not genuinely a specialized form of another type.
understand.whyItMatters: Inheritance can reduce duplication and express substitutable types, but deep or inappropriate hierarchies make code harder to understand.
understand.analogy: A specialized vehicle inherits common vehicle capabilities and adds its own features; the analogy is useful only when the subtype truly is a kind of the base type.
understand.summary: Python Inheritance and Method Overriding introduces a focused part of Python's object model and its practical use.

explain.narrative: Study the concept, trace the receiver and state for each operation, then run the examples. Pay attention to Python's conventions and documented protocol behavior rather than assuming that class syntax provides strict access control.

examples.explanation: A subclass inherits accessible base-class behavior.

examples.title: Override a method

examples.title: Extend behavior with super()
examples.explanation: super() delegates to the next class in the method resolution order.

examples.title: Check subclass relationships
examples.code:
class Vehicle: pass
class Bike(Vehicle): pass
print(issubclass(Bike, Vehicle))
examples.explanation: issubclass tests whether one class derives from another.

examples.title: Use inherited initialization
examples.explanation: Calling the base initializer establishes base-class invariants.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small program that demonstrates python inheritance and method overriding. Write down the object types, relevant attributes, method calls and expected state changes before running it.
practise.independentTask: Extend the example into a small domain model of your choice. Add validation, clear method names, boundary tests and a short explanation of why your design uses classes rather than simpler functions or data structures.
hints: Identify which object owns each piece of state.
Trace the first argument supplied to every bound method.
Prefer explicit invariants and small public interfaces.
Test at least one boundary or unsupported input.
Use composition when it models the relationship more accurately than inheritance.
practise.challenge: Refactor the model into a testable design with clear responsibilities, documented public behavior and tests for normal, boundary and invalid cases.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute on the supported Python version and match their outputs.
The implementation follows Python's documented class and special-method semantics.
State changes are scoped to the intended object or class.
Unsupported inputs produce a deliberate result or a clear exception.
The design avoids unnecessary inheritance, shared mutable defaults and misleading private-access claims.
